next_step: Finalize POC SLA + perf tests on holiday spike
summary: Enterprise contact center focused on AI-first agent assist and resilient routing for bursty traffic. Evaluating Redwood Dedicated + Optimize for holiday/marketing spikes and regulatory controls.
notes: 11/08 kickoff call w/ CTO + Head of CX. Very sensitivity to downtime during promotional spikes.
Customer quote: 'If we slow for 30m during a flash sale we lose a lot of revenue and trust'
Primary ask: deterministic tail-latency under sudden surge (10x baseline) and graceful degradation to lower-cost model without dropping requests.
Current stack: hybrid cloud (GCP primary), Genesys voice layer, proprietary ticketing db. Looking to replace clumsy webhooks w/ tool-calling for CRM updates.
Security: must support SSO (SAML), enterprise KMS, audit trails retained 1 year, regional residency (US-EAST required for PCI scope).
Finance: procurement window closes EoY; procurement insists on predictable committed spend or credits for overage.
Internal stakeholders: CTO (Anya Park), Head of CX (Liam O'Neill), Infra Lead (Marcus Chen), Procurement (Elena Ruiz).
AE notes: Prefers Redwood’s rollout features (canary/A-B) and Dedicated pools for predictable throughput; worried about POC representativeness for true holiday spikes.
timeline: 2024-10-20 - Lead created via partner referral (cloud-systems integrator)
2024-10-25 - Discovery call: mapped workloads, baseline qps ~800 reqs/s during peak, typical median latency target <150ms/token for agent assist
2024-11-01 - Security questionnaire submitted (SaaS Vendor Security Form).
2024-11-08 - Kickoff demo + Fireflies meeting (ffx_2024-11-08_torrentia_kickoff) — demo of hosted API and canary routing.
2024-11-15 - Provided pricing sketch for Dedicated pool + Optimize credits; client requested a POC plan that includes synthetic holiday spike test.

requirements: SLO: tail latency (99.9) <= 600ms for agent assist responses under 10x baseline surge
Throughput: sustain 8k reqs/s for 30 minutes (simulated flash sale), burst to 15k reqs/s for 5 minutes
Model preferences: base model family (open weights acceptable) + fallback small-quantized variant for deep degradation
Functional: tool calling to CRM (create/update tickets), structured output for agent UI, streaming responses to agent console
Security: SAML SSO, enterprise KMS support for encryption at rest, SOC2 compliance proof, audit log export to SIEM
Data residency: primary US-EAST processing; logs retained for 12 months with redaction controls
poc_plan: Week 0: Access provisioning + sample dataset load (10k historical tickets)
Week 1: Deploy Redwood Dedicated trial node in VPC, run baseline agent-assist flows (non-production)
Week 2: Implement tool-calling connector to staging CRM and verify idempotency + auth
Week 3: Synthetic spike test — ramp to 10x baseline for 30 mins; capture latency profile and dropped requests
Week 4: Run holiday-pattern test (bursty arrivals + longer context) + measure cost delta with Optimize suggestions
Deliverables: latency & cost report, configuration playbook (batching, caching, quant profiles), go/no-go decision criteria
risk_assessment: Risk: POC not reproducing production spike patterns -> Mitigation: ingest real ingress traces and run large-scale replay in staging
Risk: Key management constraints delay deployment -> Mitigation: temporary use of customer-managed cloud KMS with limited scope until HSM onboarding completes
Risk: Integration with legacy telephony/Genesys layer for routing -> Mitigation: SE-led adapter + early joint smoke tests
Risk: Procurement wants consumption cap -> Mitigation: propose committed Dedicated pool with burst credits and cost alerts
win_criteria: 99.9 latency within target during synthetic 10x spike
Tool-calling completes with idempotent updates to CRM under load
Security sign-off on KMS + audit logging
Procurement approves committed spend for Dedicated pool
